message.content: monokl changelog quality (trail 371 "Releases are rehearsed and verifiable"). The owner's review: our changesets are honest but not user-first, succinct or scannable, and nobody thinks about the whole changelog. Evidence (read crates/monokl/CHANGELOG.md on origin/main and the two pending changesets in .changeset/ that release PR #119 will consume: lean-columns and michi-0-10; find their exact filenames): (1) internals and process leak into entries: "chosen from a grid of 18 settings", "Rejected, with the measurements ... scripts/agent-cost.py (206 to 0)", decision-log section numbers; (2) repo-internal jargon: "On the 222 rows of the harness..." appears in nearly every entry, the user does not know the harness; the value ("an answer costs a fifth of the bytes") is buried after it; (3) too long to scan: five dense sub-bullets plus very long Breaking/Action paragraphs, against CONTRIBUTING's own "one idea per bullet", "short bullets"; (4) two audiences mixed: CLI/agent users and Rust library users (SearchResponse, Budget, CodeBlock fields) share entries; (5) internal changes headlined as features; (6) one story split across several entries with repeated measurements, no what's-new overview. Do, in ONE PR to main (cut `git fetch origin && git switch -c docs/user-first-changesets origin/main`): A. REWRITE the two pending changesets (frontmatter unchanged: `monokl: minor`) in this shape: bold lead-in naming the change as the user sees it + one line of value in plain words (what they can do now / what changed for them); then at most 3-4 short bullets, each one idea: why it matters, how to adopt, limits they hit; then `**Breaking:**` (old behavior -> new behavior, one or two sentences) and `**Action:**` (the exact thing to do, with the command or a before/after of the header) as separate short paragraphs; library-API notes (new public fields, signatures) go in ONE final sentence inside Breaking/Action marked for library users, so a CLI user can stop reading after the first paragraph; no 'harness', no decision-log section numbers, no script names, no grids; keep ONE headline number per entry in plain words ("about 9% fewer tokens per search" with how it was measured in half a sentence, e.g. 'measured on 222 sample questions') and move the other numbers, the rejected alternatives and the tradeoffs to the decision log, which already has them (check docs/spec/05-research-and-decisions.md sections 51 and 52; add what is missing there, do not delete content). Target: each entry <= ~12 lines rendered, scannable in 10 seconds. Keep every fact a user needs to adapt: the 8 columns ending in `relevance` and that `rank` is gone (rows are in rank order), `relevance` meaning (percent of top row), the `truncated[N]{row,field,removed}:` block and `…` replacing `(N more chars)`, the parser note. B. TIGHTEN CONTRIBUTING.md "Writing a changeset": add concrete limits and a before-you-merge step: write for the user of the CLI first; plain words, no repository-internal terms (harness, decision-log numbers, script names); one headline number at most; <= 4 bullets; Breaking/Action each <= 3 sentences, library notes last and marked; internal-only changes (refactors, new library fields nobody calls) get a `patch` or no changeset, never a headline; and 'Before merging a release PR, read the rendered changelog as a whole: is there a one-line what's-new, are related entries grouped, are measurements repeated?'. Include one good before/after example in the doc (use the lean-columns entry). C. If `just changesets` (the validation recipe; read scripts/ and the callisto config) can cheaply check a rule (e.g. forbid the word 'harness' and decision-log 'section N' references in .changeset/*.md, or max bullets), add it as a small check with a test; if it is not cheap, skip and say so (don't over-engineer). D. Do NOT edit published CHANGELOG.md history or the release PR, and do NOT touch crates/monokl/CHANGELOG.md at all (generated). Verify by exit code: `just changesets`, `just typos`, `just check-drift`, `callisto release --dry-run` if installed, and render the changelog preview if callisto can (`callisto version --dry-run`/scratch clone as in earlier work; state how you read the rendered result) and read the rendered 0.8.0 entries as a user: paste the rendered text in your report. Git: Conventional Commits; commit messages end with `Claude-Session: https://claude.ai/code/session_01AdtWVgDi4y4qCnpfdozb2n`; push; `entire trail link 371 --branch docs/user-first-changesets --base main` (never trail create / gh pr create / force-push); `gh pr ready`; PR description ends with `https://claude.ai/code/session_01AdtWVgDi4y4qCnpfdozb2n`. Owner's rule: if Entire shows a finding on this change, RESOLVE or dismiss it in Entire BEFORE pushing the fix: `entire trail finding resolve <change-ref> <ULID> -m <reason> --project gh/orin-dx`. Isolated worktree; never touch `.claude/settings.json`; network/signing/gh/entire need dangerouslyDisableSandbox. Report <=150 words plus the rendered 0.8.0 text.

---
monokl: minor
---

**A search row drops `rank` and shows `relevance` in place of `finalScore`.** The columns are now `file,lineStart,lineEnd,nodeKind,parent,symbolSignature,snippet,relevance`. On the 222 rows of the harness the total output falls from 118,601 to 107,918 `o200k_base` tokens (9.0%), the median from 448.5 to 405.5 tokens and the p90 from 1,120 to 1,033; in bytes the total falls from 385,471 to 367,483 (4.7%). Every harness score and every one-turn answer count stays at its baseline (206 of 222).

- **`rank` is gone.** It equalled the row's position in every one of the 2,038 rows measured, and rows are still printed best first.
- **`relevance` replaces `finalScore`.** It is the row's score as a whole percent of the top row's score (top row 100, rounded to the nearest whole number). It compares the rows of one query; a raw score cannot be compared across queries. A page printed with `--offset` measures against the top row of the whole result, so its first row is not 100.
- **It lines up with `--min-score`.** The cut keeps rows scoring at least `--min-score` times the top, so the rows it drops have a `relevance` below 100 times it. The help line says so: `--min-score 0 for the 2 rows below relevance 30`. The first 8 rows are kept whatever their `relevance`.
- **Rejected, with the measurements.** Merging `lineStart` and `lineEnd` breaks `scripts/agent-cost.py` (206 to 0 answerable), grouping rows by file reorders 136 of 222 queries, and one decimal of score makes the top two rows tie in 7 queries (docs/spec/05-research-and-decisions.md, section 52).

**Breaking:** The columns `rank` and `finalScore` are gone from `monokl search` output, and `relevance` is new and last. The row has 8 cells, was 9, and the last cell is an integer from 0 to 100, was a float. `SearchResponse` has a new public field, `top_score`, the best score of the whole ranking, and `SearchView` has a new public field, `min_score`, and is no longer `Eq`. The paging hint reads `--min-score 0 for the N rows below relevance P`, was `below the cut`.

**Action:** Parse rows by header name, not by position: `rank` is no longer the second to last cell. To rank-order rows, use row order. `relevance` is a percent of the top row, so use it to see how far a row is from the first, not as a score. Code that builds a `SearchResponse` must set `top_score` (`apply_budget` sets it from the ranking), and code that builds a `SearchView` must set `min_score` (`SearchView::default()` carries the default). There is no flag for the old columns.
=======
---
monokl: minor
---

**A cut cell ends in `…` and is listed in a `truncated` block.** monokl moves to `michi-core` 0.10.0. The search rows are unchanged except where a cell is over 200 characters, which in practice is a long `symbolSignature`. 23 of the 222 harness outputs (10%) have one, and the total output grows 0.5% (385,471 bytes, was 383,506). Every harness score stays at its baseline.

- **Cut cell.** The cell keeps 199 characters and ends in `…`. It used to end in `(N more chars)`.
- **`truncated` block.** After the rows, `truncated[N]{row,field,removed}:` lists each cut cell: `row` is 0-based, `field` the column, `removed` the characters cut.
- **Row budget.** `search_row_texts` counted every line after the header as a row, so the new block would have been counted as rows (a debug build panicked, a release build gave the budget a wrong count). It returns the rows only.
- **Errors.** stderr keeps its `causes[N]` lines.
- **Not added.** No `budget` or `provenance` block: about 66 tokens a response for nothing the caller lacks.

**Breaking:** A cut cell ends in `…`, not `(N more chars)`, and the output gains a `truncated[N]{row,field,removed}:` block after the rows when a cell was cut. `ToDomainError::to_domain_error` returns michi 0.10.0's `DomainError`, so a caller that names michi types needs `michi-core` 0.10.0.

**Action:** A parser of `(N more chars)` reads the `truncated` block instead. A parser that takes every indented line of the output as a row must read only the indented lines directly under the `search[N]{...}:` header, because the lines of the `truncated` block are indented too.
======
# monokl

## 0.7.0

_2026-11-16 · [compare](https://github.com/orin-dx/monokl/compare/monokl@0.6.0...monokl@0.7.0)_

### Minor Changes

- **`monokl search` prints less by default.** The default output is the rows that matter, with one snippet line each, so an answer costs about a fifth of the bytes. On the 222 rows of the harness the median output falls from 10,012 to 1,567 bytes, the 90th percentile from 13,351 to 3,997 and the total from 1,714,350 to 420,946, and every harness score stays at its baseline.

  - **Relevance cut.** A row is kept when its `finalScore` is at least 0.3 times the top row's (`--min-score FRACTION`, `0` turns the cut off). The first 8 rows are always kept when that many exist. `--max-results` caps the result on top of that, now 20 by default (was 50), and it wins over the floor of 8. `--min-score` takes 0 to 1; anything else is a usage error (exit 2).
  - **Snippet.** Each row shows its first matching line and counts the rest (`...and 2 more matching lines`). `--snippet-lines N` shows 0 to 3 lines (3 is the old snippet). `0` prints no snippet, so a variable or type row, which has no signature, shows no declaration text.
  - **Help line.** When rows were cut the help names the flag that brings them back: `showing 9 of 37; --min-score 0 or --max-results N for more, or refine with +term/-term`. It names `--max-tokens N` when the tokens ran out first. There is no `--offset` yet.
  - **Parameters.** Chosen from a grid of 18 settings (floor 3, 5 or 8; fraction 0.15, 0.2 or 0.3; cap 15 or 20) as the smallest total output that loses no harness question against the baseline. The first choice, floor 3 and cap 15, lost a member and a Rust question.
  - **Not measured.** Whether a model finds the answer in the leaner rows, and what snippet lines 2 and 3 are worth when an agent reads for context instead of answering in one turn.

  **Breaking:** The default output changed: at most 20 rows (was 50), none below 0.3 times the top score except the first 8, and one snippet line per row (was up to 3). `SearchResponse` has a new public field, `blocks_cut_by_relevance`, `Budget` has a new public field, `min_score` (and no longer implements `Eq`), `render_search` takes a `&SearchView` and `search_row_texts` a snippet length. The truncation help line is reworded.

  **Action:** To get the earlier output, run `monokl search <query> --min-score 0 --max-results 50 --snippet-lines 3`. Code that builds a `SearchResponse` or a `Budget`, or calls `render_search` or `search_row_texts`, must pass the new values: `Budget::default()` carries the new defaults, and `SearchView::default()` the new snippet length.
- **A Rust row costs fewer bytes.** On the 222 rows of the harness the total output falls from 420,764 to 383,506 bytes (8.9%). The fd Rust median falls from 1,463 to 1,322 bytes (p90 3,140 to 2,696) and the held-out Rust median from 3,258 to 2,792 (p90 4,709 to 4,058). Every harness score and every one-turn answer count stays at its baseline.

  - **Snippet.** A matched code line is shown before a comment or attribute line: a line starting with `//`, `/*`, `*/`, `* `, `#[` or `#![` (a Rust doc comment, an attribute, a JSDoc line, a comment in a body) is shown only when too few code lines matched or it is the only match. 59% of the Rust rows with a snippet showed a doc comment or an attribute. The shown lines keep their order in the block. TypeScript follows the same rule.
  - **Rust signature.** `symbolSignature` ends before the `where` clause and says `where …` in its place, so `impl<L, M, S, F> Debug for WithGracefulShutdown<L, M, S, F> where L: Debug + 'static, M: Debug, ...` becomes `impl<L, M, S, F> Debug for WithGracefulShutdown<L, M, S, F> where …`. A line of the clause that matched is a snippet line, after the code lines. The cut is where the analyzer's syntax tree puts the clause, so a `where` in a comment or a string is not one. Ranking still reads the whole signature.
  - **More lines marker.** The count of snippet lines past the shown ones reads `+3 more` (was `...and 3 more matching lines`).
  - **Not changed, with the numbers.** No signature starts with an attribute or a doc comment already. The `parent` column is `kind name` and costs 5% of the bytes. Test-path rows are 1.4% of the rows. Capping the signature length and rounding `finalScore` were measured and not taken (docs/spec/05-research-and-decisions.md, section 48).
  - **Still above the rg policy.** The fd Rust median is 1,322 bytes against 731. What remains is the floor of 8 rows.

  **Breaking:** `CodeBlock` has a new public field, `where_start`, the offset of the `where` keyword of a Rust declaration's where clause (`None` when there is none, and for TypeScript and JavaScript); code that builds a `CodeBlock` must set it. The text of a row changed. A Rust row's `symbolSignature` drops the where clause and ends in ` where …`; the snippet line is a code line where one matched, and for a Rust item a where-clause line can now be a snippet line; the marker is `+N more` instead of `...and N more matching line(s)`.

  **Action:** Set `where_start: None` where you build a `CodeBlock`. Code that parses the marker, or reads a bound out of a Rust `symbolSignature`, must change: the marker is `+N more`, and a where clause is in the file at `lineStart`–`lineEnd`. `search_row_texts` and `render_search` keep their signatures. There is no flag for the old rows.
- **Search ranks a declaration by its abbreviated name, and ranks `impl` blocks lower.** Scores and row order change; no API or wire shape changes.

  - **Abbreviated names.** A name token of at least 3 characters now matches a query term that starts with it, so `ListenerExt` holds `listener` and `extension`, and `reqIdGenFactory` holds `request`, `id`, `generator` and `factory`. A token never matches a term it is longer than (`parser` is not `parse`), and a token of 1 or 2 characters has to equal the term. A prefix match counts as much as an equal one in the name boost, including the bonus for a name that is exactly the query. Measured alone: answerable in the first three rows 204 of 222 to 206, held-out Rust 34 of 36 to 35 (axum `listener extension` from absent to rank 2), no harness set loses a hit.
  - **Impl prior.** The multiplier for a Rust `impl` block falls from 1.1 to 0.9, so the struct or method an `impl` wraps outranks the block around it. Measured alone it changes no harness count; it puts `OwnerFilter` and `is_within` ahead of their `impl` blocks and, with the prefix rule, removes a regression the prefix rule causes on fd `directory entry stripped path`. Dropping it was tried and measured worse: the prefix rule alone changes 6 first rows (3 better, 3 worse), both together change 8 (5 better, 1 equal, 2 worse).
  - **Tradeoff.** The prefix rule that fixes `ListenerExt` also matches where it should not. `RequestPartsExt` now matches `extractor` through `ext` and scores as exactly the query, so axum `extractor from request parts` no longer has `FromRequestParts` in the first five rows, and zod `global registry metadata` is worse (`meta` starts `metadata`). 47 of the 48 queries of the earlier blind review keep their first row.
- **`monokl search --offset N` prints the next page of rows.** It skips the first N ranked rows and prints the next page under the same cut and caps, so the rows the lean default hides are reachable without paying for the first ones again. The relevance cut stays relative to the top row of the whole result, so page 1 plus page 2 equals one run with a larger `--max-results`. `--max-tokens` bounds the page that is returned, not the rows skipped. An offset past the last row prints no rows and the `totalCount`, and exits 0; a non-number is a usage error (exit 2).

  - **Help line.** When rows remain it names the next value: `showing 8 of 31; next: --offset 8, or refine with +term/-term`. It replaces the `--max-results N` and `--max-tokens N` advice, which re-paid for the rows already seen; `--min-score 0 for the 20 rows below the cut` is named when the relevance cut dropped rows (the `of 31` counts those rows too), and offsets keep counting the same ranking with it. An empty page the caps caused (a row larger than the token cap) still names the cap.
  - **Library.** `Budget` and `SearchResponse` each have a new public field, `offset`, so code that builds them must set it (`Budget::default()` has 0).
  - **Stateless.** Every call re-runs the search. Pages are exact for an unchanged tree.

### Patch Changes

- **`monokl search` opens each matching source file once.** Text search keeps the text of a matching file of at most 256 KiB, up to 16 MiB over all files, and analysis uses it instead of opening the file again. On a tree of 20,000 small matching files the search takes about a quarter less time, and peak memory rises by at most that 16 MiB. The output is byte-identical. A file over 256 KiB, or past the 16 MiB, is opened again as before.

## 0.6.0

_2026-11-15 · [compare](https://github.com/orin-dx/monokl/compare/monokl@0.5.0...monokl@0.6.0)_

### Minor Changes

- Blocks carry the byte span they cover and the position of the block that encloses them, so later stages can tell blocks apart by where they are and not by their text.

  - **Span.** `CodeBlock::span` is the byte range of the analyzed source the block covers, so `source[span] == code`. Offsets count bytes of the text the analyzer received, which is the lossy UTF-8 decoding of a file with invalid bytes.
  - **Parent.** `CodeBlock::parent_index` is the position of the enclosing block in `FileAnalysis::blocks` followed by `FileAnalysis::test_blocks`. It is set exactly when `parent` is, for the members of a class, object literal, `impl`, trait or inline module.
  - **No change to results.** Nothing reads either field yet: `monokl search` output and the harness scores are unchanged.

  **Breaking:** `CodeBlock` has two new public fields. Code that builds one must set `span` and `parent_index`.
- Blocks carry the name their analyzer read from the syntax tree, and the name boost in `monokl search` uses it instead of cutting the signature text.

  - **Name from the tree.** `CodeBlock::name` is the declared identifier of a function, class, interface, type alias, enum, namespace, method, property or constant, and the target of an `impl` (`Trait for Target` for a trait impl). It is `None` for a re-export, an anonymous default export, a destructuring declaration, a macro call and an `extern` block, which get no name boost.
  - **Scores can change.** `finalScore` differs only where the old text head held a word the name does not, such as a modifier (`get`, `static`) or a variable's type, and for `export default Button;`, which declares no name. No column is added and the harness scores are unchanged: identifier 58/59, questions 17/18, members 15/16, Rust fd 22/24, held-out 23/24 and 12/12.
  - **Library.** `CodeBlock` has a new public field, so code that builds one must set `name`. `rank::name_match_boost` reads `block.name`, not the signature or the first line of `code`.

  Breaking: construct `CodeBlock` with a `name` field.
- **A match is credited to the block it sits in.** `monokl search` decides which block holds a matching line by where in the line each match starts, not by comparing the text of the line, so a match is never given to a block that only shares its line, and a line a block covers is never lost.

  - **Why it matters.** A class or object keeps a match that is its own even when a method on the same line matches another term, and blocks that share a line (`} b() {`, `}, // note`, `const a = 1; const needle = 2;`) are told apart by the byte where the match begins. A test function and the module that holds it are never both credited.
  - **Terms are searched one by one.** `regex:class.* m` finds the method `m` that starts on the line `class.*` matches; the terms used to be joined, and the first match hid the second.
  - **End of a declaration.** `regex:$` and other matches at the end of a declaration belong to it.
  - **Output.** Same columns and the same order. On the pinned repositories the shown rows are identical, `totalCount` is 1 to 3 lower in a few queries, and `finalScore` moves in its later digits where fewer blocks change the document frequencies. Harness scores are unchanged.

- **What changes on the wire.** A cell over michi's 200-character cap used to end in `(N more chars)`. It now keeps 199 characters, ends in `…`, and a `truncated[N]{row,field,removed}:` block after the rows lists each cut (`row` is 0-based, `removed` is the characters cut). In practice only `symbolSignature` reaches the cap, because the snippet lines are already cut at 160 characters by monokl. The rest of the output is byte-identical.
- **Measured.** 23 of the 222 harness outputs (10%) carry the block. The total output is 385,471 bytes, was 383,506 at the last measure on main (+0.5%, about +85 bytes on an affected output). The harness holds: identifiers 59/59, questions 17/18, members 15/16, Rust 22/24, held-out 32/33, 22/22 and 35/36, answerable in one turn 206/222.
- **Why accept it.** The block is michi's definition of a cut and says what the reader did not get; the old suffix could not be told from a signature that ended that way. Cutting in monokl would hand-roll what michi provides (AGENTS.md) and drop the count. The cost is small and falls on the longest signatures.
- **Rejected.** Raising the cap to avoid the block: a longer signature costs more on every row that has one, to save the block on a few. Cutting the signature in monokl before michi sees it: no block, but the reader cannot tell a cut signature from a whole one. Adding `truncation_hint`: it tells the reader to pass `full=true`, which monokl has no flag for.
- **Not adopted from 0.10.0.** `BudgetSummary` and `ProvenanceBlock` cost about 66 tokens a response (+13% on the 509-token mean of a 20-query sample) and replace no line. Their types are marked unstable by michi until a second consumer uses them. `Section` is used for the one `search` list, which is how `total_count` is set now that `AgentResponse::total_count` is gone. `PartialSuccess` is per operation of a batch; a search has no operations.

With the `truncated` block that counted its lines as rows, so a debug build panicked on `each block needs its printed row` (`zustand "create store state"`) and a release build gave the budget a wrong row count. It now reads the indented lines under the header only.
- **Errors.** michi 0.8 made `DomainError::from_error` keep only the error's own message. monokl calls `from_error_with_causes`, so `causes[N]` is still printed and a multi-line message stays whole. Supersedes the `from_error` wording of the michi entry above.

- **Decision.** The row columns are `file,lineStart,lineEnd,nodeKind,parent,symbolSignature,snippet,relevance`. `rank` is gone. `finalScore` is replaced by `relevance`: the row's score as an integer percent of the top row's score (top row 100, rounded to the nearest whole number, clamped to 0..=100). The float score stays in core for the sort and the relevance cut; `SearchResponse::top_score` carries the best score of the whole ranking, so a page after `--offset` still measures against the first row of the result. The output layer computes the percent from `final_score` and `top_score`, the floats the sort and the cut use, never from printed text. A top score that is not positive leaves nothing to divide by; every row then ties with the top under the cut (the threshold is 0), so each shows 100. No other column, no order and no lean default changed.
- **Name.** `relevance`: columns are camelCase words (`lineStart`, `symbolSignature`, `nodeKind`), and one lower-case word fits that; `scorePct` would have named the unit instead of the meaning and nothing in michi's field handling needed it. The `--min-score` help, the README and the paging hint use the same word: the hint says `--min-score 0 for the 2 rows below relevance 30`, where 30 is 100 times `--min-score` (rounded to a whole number).
- **It lines up with the cut.** The cut keeps a row with `score >= min_score * top`, so a kept row shows at least `100 * min_score` and the rows the cut dropped show less. Two exceptions, both stated in the docs: the first 8 rows are kept whatever their score, so a printed row can be under the line, and a row within half a point below the line rounds up onto it.
- **Why.** A column-economics study of the 222 harness queries (2,038 rows, `o200k_base` tokens) found:
  - `rank` equals the row index in 2,038 of 2,038 rows and is 3.8% of the tokens. A reader has the position already. Nothing in `scripts/rg-compare.py` or `scripts/agent-cost.py` reads it.
  - `finalScore` is 9.2% of the tokens, as 6-decimal floats, and nothing in the scripts reads it. The ratio of the top two scores is informative (AUC 0.80 for telling whether the first row is the answer; a ratio of 1.5 or more flags 118 queries as clear, with 94% precision) but absolute scores are not comparable across queries (BM25 depends on the corpus). So the score is kept as a share of the top row, which carries the ratio and drops the digits.
- **Rejected.**
  - *Merge `lineStart` and `lineEnd` into one `lines` cell.* Saves tokens but breaks `scripts/agent-cost.py`, whose row pattern needs `file,lineStart,lineEnd` first: one-turn answerable falls from 206 to 0. It would also change the shape every reader parses.
  - *`lineStart` plus a span length.* Same break, and a reader has to add to get the end line.
  - *A short `nodeKind`.* Judgment, not measured: it saves a few bytes a row and adds a lookup, and the full words are the ones a model already knows.
  - *Blank repeated files.* Judgment, not measured: a row that repeats the file above it leaves the cell empty. Rows are read one at a time and a reader that sees an empty cell cannot tell it from a missing value.

default:
    @just --list

    cargo install cargo-nextest cargo-llvm-cov cargo-machete cargo-mutants cargo-deny typos-cli zizmor --locked

    proto install
    moon sync vcs-hooks

    cargo llvm-cov nextest --workspace --all-features --locked --html --open

    cargo fmt --all --check

#!/usr/bin/env python3
"""Fails when a pending changeset breaks a rule of CONTRIBUTING.md's "Writing a changeset" that a script can judge:
no repository-internal terms (the harness, decision-log section numbers, script names, parameter grids) and at most
MAX_BULLETS bullets. Wording and length are left to review. Run as `python3 -I scripts/check-changesets.py [FILE...]`;
with no files it checks `.changeset/*.md` except the README.
"""

import re
import sys
from pathlib import Path

MAX_BULLETS = 4

# (pattern, what to say instead). Matched outside the frontmatter, case-insensitively.
FORBIDDEN = [
    (r"\bharness\b", "the harness is repository-internal; say what was measured, e.g. 'measured on 222 sample questions'"),
    (r"(?:§|\bsections?\s+\d)", "decision-log section numbers belong in docs/spec/05-research-and-decisions.md"),
    (r"\b[\w-]+\.(?:py|sh)\b", "script names are repository-internal"),
    (r"\bgrid of\b", "parameter grids belong in the decision log"),
    (r"docs/(?:spec|adr|architecture)/", "repository doc paths belong in the decision log"),
]
BULLET = re.compile(r"^\s*(?:[-*+]|\d+\.)\s")


def body(text):
    """The changeset text after its `---` frontmatter."""
    parts = text.split("---", 2)
    return parts[2] if text.startswith("---") and len(parts) == 3 else text


def problems(name, text):
    """One message per rule `text` breaks; empty when it passes."""
    found = []
    lines = body(text).splitlines()
    for number, line in enumerate(lines, 1):
        for pattern, advice in FORBIDDEN:
            match = re.search(pattern, line, re.IGNORECASE)
            if match:
                found.append(f"{name}: '{match.group(0)}' in the body, line {number}: {advice}")
    bullets = sum(1 for line in lines if BULLET.match(line))
    if bullets > MAX_BULLETS:
        found.append(f"{name}: {bullets} bullets, at most {MAX_BULLETS}")
    return found


def main(argv):
    root = Path(__file__).resolve().parent.parent
    files = [Path(a) for a in argv] or sorted(
        p for p in (root / ".changeset").glob("*.md") if p.name != "README.md"
    )
    found = [message for path in files for message in problems(path.name, path.read_text(encoding="utf-8"))]
    for message in found:
        print(message, file=sys.stderr)
    return 1 if found else 0


if __name__ == "__main__":
    sys.exit(main(sys.argv[1:]))
EOF

            [m.split(" in the body")[0] for m in CC.problems("a.md", GOOD + "On the 222 rows of the Harness.\n")],

        for text in ("breaks `scripts/agent-cost.py`", "run check.sh", "chosen from a grid of 18 settings",

            with self.subTest(text=text):
                self.assertTrue(CC.problems("a.md", GOOD + text + "\n"))

        text = FRONT + "**Lead.** Value.\n\n" + "- Bullet.\n" * 5
        self.assertEqual(CC.problems("a.md", text), ["a.md: 5 bullets, at most 4"])

    def test_four_bullets_pass_and_sub_bullets_count(self):
        self.assertEqual(CC.problems("a.md", FRONT + "- a\n" * 4), [])
        self.assertEqual(CC.problems("a.md", FRONT + "- a\n- b\n- c\n- d\n  - e\n"), ["a.md: 5 bullets, at most 4"])

    def test_frontmatter_is_not_checked(self):
        self.assertEqual(CC.problems("a.md", "---\nharness: minor\n---\n\nBody.\n"), [])

    def test_main_exit_code_follows_the_files(self):
        with tempfile.TemporaryDirectory() as directory:
            good, bad = Path(directory, "good.md"), Path(directory, "bad.md")
            good.write_text(GOOD)
            bad.write_text(GOOD + "harness\n")
            self.assertEqual(CC.main([str(good)]), 0)
            self.assertEqual(CC.main([str(good), str(bad)]), 1)

    def test_pending_changesets_pass(self):
        self.assertEqual(CC.main([]), 0)


if __name__ == "__main__":
    unittest.main()

deny:
    cargo deny check

machete:

name: CI

on:
  push:
    branches: [main]
  pull_request:
  merge_group:

permissions:
  contents: read

# Pull requests cancel their own superseded runs. A push to main or a merge group gets a group per commit: GitHub keeps
# one pending run per group and cancels the rest, which would leave a merged commit unchecked.
concurrency:
  group: ${{ github.workflow }}-${{ github.event_name == 'pull_request' && github.ref || github.sha }}
  cancel-in-progress: ${{ github.event_name == 'pull_request' }}

env:
  CARGO_TERM_COLOR: always
  CARGO_INCREMENTAL: "0"
  RUST_BACKTRACE: 1

# Each job runs `just` recipes, so `just ci` locally does what CI does.
jobs:
  lint:
    name: Lint
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@3d3c42e5aac5ba805825da76410c181273ba90b1 # v7.0.1
        with:
          persist-credentials: false
      - id: rust
        run: |
          version=$(sed -n 's/^rust = "\(.*\)"/\1/p' .prototools)
          test -n "$version"
          echo "version=$version" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"
      - uses: orin-dx/actions/setup-rust@2521888266780dabc7f5fd4c32b02d6ab82849db # v1.1
        with:
          toolchain: ${{ steps.rust.outputs.version }}
          components: clippy,rustfmt
      - uses: taiki-e/install-action@cfdb7ed4ccc7c7dce37759eae89dc5674b469b39 # v2.90.3
        with:
          tool: just,cargo-machete,typos
      - run: just lint doc-check machete typos

  test:
    name: Test / ${{ matrix.os }}
    runs-on: ${{ matrix.os }}
    strategy:
      fail-fast: false
      matrix:
        os: [ubuntu-latest, macos-latest]
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@3d3c42e5aac5ba805825da76410c181273ba90b1 # v7.0.1
        with:
          persist-credentials: false
      - id: rust
        run: |
          version=$(sed -n 's/^rust = "\(.*\)"/\1/p' .prototools)
          test -n "$version"
          echo "version=$version" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"
      - uses: orin-dx/actions/setup-rust@2521888266780dabc7f5fd4c32b02d6ab82849db # v1.1
        with:
          toolchain: ${{ steps.rust.outputs.version }}
      - uses: taiki-e/install-action@cfdb7ed4ccc7c7dce37759eae89dc5674b469b39 # v2.90.3
        with:
          tool: just,cargo-nextest
      - run: just test

  msrv:
    name: MSRV
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@3d3c42e5aac5ba805825da76410c181273ba90b1 # v7.0.1
        with:
          persist-credentials: false
      - id: msrv
        run: echo "version=$(sed -n 's/^rust-version = "\(.*\)"/\1/p' Cargo.toml)" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"
      - uses: orin-dx/actions/setup-rust@2521888266780dabc7f5fd4c32b02d6ab82849db # v1.1
        with:
          toolchain: ${{ steps.msrv.outputs.version }}
      - run: cargo check --workspace --all-targets --all-features --locked

  coverage:
    name: Coverage
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@3d3c42e5aac5ba805825da76410c181273ba90b1 # v7.0.1
        with:
          persist-credentials: false
      - id: rust
        run: |
          version=$(sed -n 's/^rust = "\(.*\)"/\1/p' .prototools)
          test -n "$version"
          echo "version=$version" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"
      - uses: orin-dx/actions/setup-rust@2521888266780dabc7f5fd4c32b02d6ab82849db # v1.1
        with:
          toolchain: ${{ steps.rust.outputs.version }}
          components: llvm-tools-preview
      - uses: taiki-e/install-action@cfdb7ed4ccc7c7dce37759eae89dc5674b469b39 # v2.90.3
        with:
          tool: just,cargo-nextest,cargo-llvm-cov
      - run: just coverage
      - uses: actions/upload-artifact@cf430e030ddbb5b0abf93d22962f4752f3646cd9 # v7.0.2
        if: always()
        with:
          name: coverage
          path: lcov.info
          retention-days: 14

  audit:
    name: Audit
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@3d3c42e5aac5ba805825da76410c181273ba90b1 # v7.0.1
        with:
          persist-credentials: false
      - uses: taiki-e/install-action@cfdb7ed4ccc7c7dce37759eae89dc5674b469b39 # v2.90.3
        with:
          tool: just,cargo-deny,zizmor@1.29.0
      - run: just deny zizmor check-drift

  changesets:
    name: Changesets
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@3d3c42e5aac5ba805825da76410c181273ba90b1 # v7.0.1
        with:
          fetch-depth: 0
          persist-credentials: false
      - uses: orin-dx/callisto/.github/actions/callisto-validate@aebeedcdaa1dce8f0d9ad1836844ab6be68daf1f # callisto@0.20.0

  # The one check to require in branch protection.
  ci:
    name: CI
    needs: [lint, test, msrv, coverage, audit, changesets]
    if: always()
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    steps:
      - if: contains(needs.*.result, 'failure') || contains(needs.*.result, 'cancelled')
        run: exit 1

  # Runs only after a merge. The merge queue should keep main green; this catches whatever slips past it.
  main-red:
    name: Main is red
    needs: [ci]
    if: always() && github.event_name == 'push' && needs.ci.result == 'failure'
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    permissions:
      issues: write
    steps:
      - env:
          GH_TOKEN: ${{ github.token }}
          GH_REPO: ${{ github.repository }}
          RUN_URL: ${{ github.server_url }}/${{ github.repository }}/actions/runs/${{ github.run_id }}
          SHA: ${{ github.sha }}
        run: |
          body="CI failed on main at $SHA: $RUN_URL"
          number=$(gh issue list --label ci-red --state open --json number --jq '.[0].number // empty')
          if [ -n "$number" ]; then
            gh issue comment "$number" --body "$body"
          else
            gh label create ci-red --color B60205 --description "CI failed on main" 2>/dev/null || true
            gh issue create --label ci-red --title "CI is red on main" --body "$body"
          fi
          echo "::error::$body"
          exit 1
